Alicia (support): Heads-up — tenant `acme-inc` is hitting customer-facing decrypt failures after yesterday's KMS key rotation. Getting a flood of 403s in the API and a billing spike from retries. Root error from client: `AccessDeniedException: EncryptionContextMismatch`

Ben (oncall): Ticket link: https://support.redwood.ai/t/78432 — saw the same in staging a bit earlier. Any chance the rotation swapped aliases and we lost a grant? :eyes:

Alicia (support): Error payload from our proxy logs: 
```
{"error":"AccessDeniedException","message":"EncryptionContext value does not match","ciphertext_blob":"...","request_id":"r-0c12"}
```
Also noticed requests for this tenant are ~2x slower (retries). Some clients fall back to older codepaths and bill us more tokens.

Carol (security): EncryptionContextMismatch usually means the encryption context sent to KMS at decrypt time is different from encrypt time. Two quick suspects: 1) proxy or client is dropping/truncating the encctx header 2) key policy now requires a tag/condition that isn't present in STS session.

Dave (infra): I pulled a proxied request from the same timeframe and saw the encryption-context header absent in the proxied POST to our KMS proxy: 
```
POST /kms/decrypt
Headers: {"content-type":"application/json"}
Body: {"CiphertextBlob":"..."}
// expected: "EncryptionContext":{"tenant":"acme-inc"}
```
Looks like header stripping on the edge LB -> proxy hop for requests >32KB. Repro: curl with large metadata keeps encctx, but our internal nginx set `underscores_in_headers off` and we saw it drop when header encoded differently.

Eve (sre): That could explain latency too — clients retry client-side on AccessDenied. Are we seeing any STS assume-role failures tied to role session tags? CloudTrail shows decrypt calls succeeded for other tenants at same time. Filtered logs: `Decrypt` failing only for tenant with encctx present.

KMSBot: Grant propagation check: 1) CMK alias arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd rotated 2026-03-10T02:15Z 2) Active grants: 0 for principal arn:aws:iam::111111111:role/redwood-tenant-acme 3) Last key policy update: 2026-03-10T02:14Z (rotation script)

Carol (security): If grants are 0, and rotation replaced the key material, the existing grant tokens would be invalid. But Grant absence alone usually gives NotFound/AccessDenied at the key level, not encctx mismatch. Combined symptoms -> proxy is stripping encctx for this tenant and key policy requires encctx (conditional).

Ben (oncall): Quick mitigation options: 1) Roll back alias to previous CMK (if available) 2) Create temporary fallback key without encctx restrictions and pin tenant to it 3) Patch proxy to preserve encctx header for large requests (hotfix)

Alicia (support): Customer is impacted -> they want a rollback now. Which is fastest?

Dave (infra): Rollback takes ~10-15m if we restore alias to previous key material (we can only if previous material preserved and not scheduled for deletion). Creating fallback key and updating tenant mapping is safer but requires config deploy (~20m). Proxy patch is low-risk but slower to ship to prod pipeline (~45m).

Eve (sre): Also need to be careful with audit trails — any rollback or fallback must be logged to meet retention/compliance. We should attach a CloudTrail marker and create an incident note.

Carol (security): Before any change: I need a minimal repro with full headers from a failing request. Alicia — can you attach a redacted full HTTP request (no ciphertext) including all headers? We need to prove encctx is missing on the wire to KMS.

Alicia (support): Pasted a sanitized request to the ticket (linked). TL;DR: our edge sends `x-encryption-context` but nginx upstream converts to `encryptioncontext` (no dash) and our proxy only looks for exact key.

Dave (infra): That's the bug. Our proxy expects `EncryptionContext` in JSON body or `x-aws-encryption-context` header. Nginx rewrite removed the dash. Quick fix: add `proxy_set_header X-AWS-ENCRYPTION-CONTEXT $http_x_encryption_context;` and preserve case. I'll prepare a canary patch to edge for one region.

Ben (oncall): Can we do the canary now for us-east-1 small prod shard?

Dave (infra): Deploying canary to us-east-1 now. ETA ~7m. Rolling only the edge layer config, not the proxy.

Alicia (support): Customer confirmed decreased errors on canary region for their requests routed there. :thumbsup:

Carol (security): After canary validates for 30m, we should: 1) rollout edge fix globally 2) run a scan to detect any other tenants whose headers were transformed 3) consider adding a defensive server-side check: if encryptioncontext missing but tenant header present, reject earlier with clearer auditable log.

Eve (sre): I'll create the incident doc and retention tag. Also scheduling a retro to review the rotation script and key policy coupling to header names. We should avoid tight policy coupling to fragile header formats.

KMSBot: Audit note: created event 2026-03-12T03:20Z incident-78432. CloudTrail entry ids attached.

Alicia (support): Customer updated: back to normal on canary, will wait for global rollout. Thanks team.

Ben (oncall): Follow-ups: - Confirm previous CMK state is archived - Add unit test in rotation script to assert no encctx policy conditions that rely on header formatting - Add alert for sudden increase in retried decrypt errors

Carol (security): Agreed. Also file a proposal to use envelope metadata in token rather than fragile headers for encryption context.

Dave (infra): Global rollout started. Will post when complete.

Alicia (support): Completed — customer verified. Closing escalation but tagging for retro. :white_check_mark:
